summary: MCP launcher, runtime diagnostic, and dispatch-readiness tools.

tools.notes: Read-only validation of an unpersisted proposed work-record dispatch contract. It does not mutate canonical records or admission evidence.
use_when: Operator needs readiness diagnostics for a proposed record before it is persisted.
do_not_use_when: The record is canonical; use workspace_validate_dispatch with its durable unit identifier.
authoritative_for: structural preflight of caller-supplied proposed record content

tools.display_name: Workspace Chassis Control Engine admission runtime diagnostic
tools.notes: Read-only agent-safe MCP route that diagnoses the running MCP server process (not the caller shell) for Chassis Control Engine worker_admission_v1 runtime config. Reports only source names and booleans (service URL, API key, worker-admission route, request-contract digest presence, and whether the remote-admission observability path is loaded); never returns any secret value, route value, digest, key hash, bearer material, project id, or request/response body.
use_when: Diagnose the running server process's admission configuration.
do_not_use_when: The task inspects caller-shell configuration, needs a secret value, or asks for admission or policy permission.

tools.notes: Read-only introspection for the dispatch caller/session identity and bootstrap review contract. Identity authority must be launcher- or transport-minted; caller-supplied role identity is refused. Reports the current bootstrap state (bootstrap_exception_active / bootstrap_review_missing / bootstrap_exception_consumed). workspace_agent_dispatch is the active supported MCP dispatch surface. Its dispatch_selection read keeps role required, because it asks about one named selection rather than starting a canonical unit.
use_when: Check which dispatch caller identity and bootstrap review state the launcher minted for this session.
Ask whether one named dispatch_selection (role and subject) would route, without starting it.
do_not_use_when: Starting a canonical unit; call workspace_agent_dispatch, which derives the role from the unit.
dispatch_readiness for a known unit; use workspace_validate_dispatch.
authoritative_for: dispatch caller identity and bootstrap review state introspection

recommended_first_call.operation: read the minted dispatch caller identity and bootstrap state

paid_cce.notes: Read-only introspection for the dispatch caller/session identity and bootstrap review contract. Identity authority must be launcher- or transport-minted; caller-supplied role identity is refused. Reports the current bootstrap state (bootstrap_exception_active / bootstrap_review_missing / bootstrap_exception_consumed), and under a valid paid/CCE key posture the graph_impact_persistence_unavailable state for graph-impact evidence persistence prerequisites. workspace_agent_dispatch is the active supported MCP dispatch surface.

tools.notes: Structural dispatch readiness for a WK or slice; it never launches an agent, mutates canonical records, or decides CCE policy. dispatch_role is implementation (worker readiness) or read_only; omit it for a role-agnostic question. Reviewer and redteam dispatch do not use this route. A managed worker needs an explicit existing implementation slice. Implementation units with absent or incomplete controlled_acceptance_state return proof-authoring correction; complete or opted_out continue. Follow returned selected-detail and proof-owner calls. Starting a canonical unit through workspace_agent_dispatch performs this readiness internally through the same owner, so this route answers an explicit "can this start?" question and is not a required pre-call.
use_when: The prospective question "can this unit start?", asked without asking to start it
do_not_use_when: dispatch_role_call: a start request goes to workspace_agent_dispatch, which runs readiness internally; this route is optional and grants no launch permission
initiative_next_action before a unit is selected
requires_prior_state: dispatch_role implementation for worker readiness or read_only for read-only readiness; omitted when role-agnostic
No dispatch depends on this call: it is an optional prospective assessment, and its result is neither permission to launch nor a substitute for the checks dispatch performs

paid_cce.notes: Structural dispatch readiness for a WK or slice; not managed-launch capability. A managed worker needs an explicit existing implementation slice. When required graph impact is stale or missing, it refreshes current-HEAD graph data and may write only ignored code-index cache, lock, temporary and candidate artifacts; candidates are never reused or authoritative. It never mutates canonical WK/evidence, admission sidecars, lifecycle, runtime, dispatch, or result state, and never launches an agent. The strict request accepts no verbose or bulk alias. Its one response keeps typed graph failures, relevant reasons, selected-owner detail calls, and the complete CCE recovery carrier; oversized output uses bounded selected detail calls. It carries only actually returned CCE judgments: local output reports measured blast-radius and decomposition facts but no CCE verdict, threshold, or paid permission. node_engine_admissibility:true requests CCE implementation admissibility for a structurally dispatchable unit; only CCE can admit, with no local admit fallback.
